title: Placement Question Schema
description: Place items into anchored gaps in a structured passage. Each placement entry pairs a gap-marker number with the item that belongs in it. Distractors are extra items with no correct gap; passage gap-markers without a corresponding placement entry are decoy positions (TOEFL Sentence Insertion variant).

placementUnit.description: Display granularity hint and marker-placement convention. 'sentence' — markers appear inline within prose; the renderer shows an inline drop slot at each marker. 'paragraph' — each marker is the entire content of its paragraph (surrounded by blank lines or at start/end of the passage); the renderer shows a block-level drop slot between paragraphs. 'sectionLabel' — each marker appears at the start of a paragraph (followed by the section's content); the renderer attaches a label slot to that paragraph's leading edge. The 'sectionLabel' value covers both real headings (IELTS Matching Headings) and analytical meta-labels (e.g., labelling each paragraph 'thesis', 'counter-argument'). Consumers MAY render uniformly regardless. Word-level placement is covered by wordBankCloze.

passage.description: Structured text with @@@1, @@@2, ... gap markers (1-based, sequential where possible). Marker-placement convention varies by placementUnit; see that field's description.

placements.description: Each entry pairs a gap-marker number with the item that belongs in it. Order is author-free; each entry is self-describing via its `gap` field. The number of placements need not equal the number of @@@N markers in the passage — extra unanswered markers are valid as decoy positions (TOEFL Sentence Insertion variant).

gap.description: 1-based gap-marker number, matching a @@@N marker in the passage.

item.description: The content that belongs in the named gap.

distractors.description: Extra items with no correct gap (decoy items). Optional. Distinct from decoy gaps — see the `placements` description. The choice pool a consumer presents in each gap dropdown is the union of `placements[].item` values and these distractors; consumers MUST randomise the order of that pool when rendering — see NORMATIVE §5.6.

allowPartialCredit.description: Award partial credit per correct gap instead of all-or-nothing.
